chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Sālim, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, who said:

I said to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, we relate in Iraq that ʿAlī عليه السلام performed salat over Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, and said six takbirs over him; then he turned to those who were behind him and said: He had been one of those at Badr.

He said: Then Jaʿfar said: It was not like that. Rather, he performed salat over him with five takbirs, then he lifted him and walked with him for a while, then placed him down and said five takbirs over him. He did that five times, until he had said twenty-five takbirs over him. And it is possible that by his saying four he meant to report what is said between the takbirs of du'a, because after the fifth takbir there is no du'a; rather, by it one departs from the جنازة. This indicates that.

key_terms.الدُّعَاءِ: the supplications recited between the takbirs
key_terms.الْجِنَازَةِ: the funeral bier or deceased over whom the prayer is performed
key_terms.الْخَامِسَةَ: the fifth takbir, after which no du'a is recited
key_terms.بَدْرِيًّا: one who participated in the Battle of Badr
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةً: a single takbir uttered in funeral prayer
key_terms.خَمْسًا: five takbirs, the number affirmed in the report
key_terms.سِتًّا: six takbirs, as mentioned in the reported claim being corrected

ai.seo_question: How many takbirs are said in salat over the deceased according to this hadith from al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the number of takbirs in salat over the deceased and corrects a reported account about Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام praying over Sahl ibn Ḥunayf. Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام explains that the prayer itself consisted of five takbirs each time, repeated on multiple occasions as the bier was carried and set down, resulting in a total of twenty-five takbirs.
